sentences.en: JACK: I've still got loads to do for our report on nutritional food labels
sentences.zh: JACK: 我们关于营养食品标签的报告还有很多工作要做。

sentences.en: ALICE: Me too
sentences.zh: ALICE: 我也是。

sentences.en: What did you learn from doing the project about your own shopping habits?
sentences.zh: 你从这个项目中对自己的购物习惯有什么新认识？

sentences.en: JACK: Well, I've always had to check labels for traces of peanuts in everything I eat because of my allergy
sentences.zh: JACK: 嗯，由于我对花生过敏，我一直以来都必须检查所有食物标签上是否含有微量花生成分。

sentences.en: But beyond that I've never really been concerned enough to check how healthy a product is
sentences.zh: 但除此之外，我从未真正足够重视去查看某种产品的健康程度。

sentences.en: ALICE: This project has actually taught me to read the labels much more carefully. tended to believe claims on packaging like 'low in fat'
sentences.zh: ALICE: 这个项目实际上教会了我更仔细地阅读食品标签。过去我倾向于相信包装上的宣传语，比如‘低脂’。

sentences.en: But I now realise that the 'healthy' yoghurt I've bought for years is full of sugar and that it's actually quite high in calories
sentences.zh: 但我现在意识到，我多年来一直购买的所谓‘健康’酸奶其实含糖量很高，而且热量实际上相当高。

sentences.en: JACK: Ready meals are the worst .. comparing the labels on supermarket pizzas was a real eye-opener
sentences.zh: JACK: 即食餐是最糟糕的……对比超市里各种披萨的标签真让我大开眼界。

sentences.en: Did you have any idea how many calories they contain? was amazed
sentences.zh: 你之前知道它们含有多少卡路里吗？我当时非常惊讶。

sentences.en: ALICE: Yes, because unless you read the label really carefully, you wouldn't know that the nutritional values given are for half a pizza
sentences.zh: ALICE: 是的，因为除非你非常仔细地阅读标签，否则你不会发现所标注的营养数值仅针对半块披萨。

sentences.en: JACK: When most people eat the whole pizza
sentences.zh: JACK: 而大多数人吃的是整块披萨。

sentences.en: Not exactly transparent is it?
sentences.zh: 这显然不够透明，对吧？

sentences.en: ALICE: Not at all
sentences.zh: ALICE: 完全不透明。

sentences.en: But I expect it won't stop you from buying pizza?
sentences.zh: 但我想这应该不会阻止你买披萨吧？

sentences.en: JACK: Probably not, no!
sentences.zh: JACK: 可能确实不会！

sentences.en: I thought comparing the different labelling systems used by food manufacturers was interesting
sentences.zh: 我觉得比较不同食品制造商所采用的各种标签体系很有意思。

sentences.en: I think the kind of labelling system used makes a big difference
sentences.zh: 我认为所采用的标签体系类型影响很大。

sentences.en: ALICE: Which one did you prefer?
sentences.zh: ALICE: 你最喜欢哪一种？

sentences.en: JACK: liked the traditional daily value system best - the one which tells you what proportion of your required daily intake of each ingredient the product contains
sentences.zh: JACK: 我最喜欢传统的每日参考值体系——即标明该产品所含每种成分占人体每日所需摄入量比例的体系。

sentences.en: I'm not sure it's 024 the easiest for people to use but at least you get the full story
sentences.zh: 我不确定它是否最容易被大众使用，但至少它提供了完整信息。

sentences.en: I like to know all the ingredients in a product - not just how much fat, salt and sugar they contain
sentences.zh: 我想了解产品中的全部成分，而不仅仅是脂肪、盐和糖的含量。

sentences.en: ALICE: But it's good supermarkets have been making an effort to provide reliable information for customers
sentences.zh: ALICE: 但超市确实在努力为顾客提供可靠的信息，这点值得肯定。

sentences.en: JACK: Yes
sentences.zh: JACK: 是的。

sentences.en: There just needs to be more consistency between labelling systems used by different supermarkets, in terms of portion sizes, etc
sentences.zh: 不过，不同超市所采用的标签体系之间还需在份量标准等方面进一步统一。

sentences.en: ALICE: Mmm
sentences.zh: ALICE: 嗯。

sentences.en: The labels on the different brands of chicken flavour crisps were quite revealing too, weren't they?
sentences.zh: 不同品牌的鸡肉味薯片标签也相当有启发性，对吧？

sentences.en: JACK: Yeah
sentences.zh: JACK: 没错。

sentences.en: I don't understand how they can get away with calling them chicken flavour
sentences.zh: 我不明白他们怎么能称其为‘鸡肉味’。

sentences.en: when they only contain artificial additives
sentences.zh: 因为其中只含有人工添加剂。

sentences.en: ALICE: know
sentences.zh: ALICE: 我知道。

sentences.en: I'd at least have expected them to contain a small percentage of real chicken
sentences.zh: 我至少希望它们含有少量真正的鸡肉。

sentences.en: JACK: Absolutely
sentences.zh: JACK: 完全同意。

sentences.en: ALICE: I think having nutritional food labeling has been a good idea, don't you? think it will change people's behaviour and stop mothers, in particular, buying the wrong things
sentences.zh: ALICE: 我觉得实行营养食品标签是个好主意，你不这么认为吗？我认为这会改变人们的行为，尤其能防止母亲们买错东西。

sentences.en: JACK: But didn't that study kind of prove the opposite?
sentences.zh: JACK: 但那项研究不是恰恰证明了相反的结果吗？

sentences.en: People didn't necessarily stop buying unhealthy products
sentences.zh: 人们未必因此停止购买不健康的产品。

sentences.en: ALICE: They only said that might be the case
sentences.zh: ALICE: 他们只是说可能存在这种情况。

sentences.en: Those findings weren't that conclusive and it was quite a small-scale study
sentences.zh: 那些研究结果并不十分确凿，而且是一项规模较小的研究。

sentences.en: I think more research has to be done
sentences.zh: 我认为还需要开展更多研究。

sentences.en: JACK: Yes, I think you're probably right
sentences.zh: JACK: 是的，我想你说得可能没错。

sentences.en: JACK: What do you think of the traffic-light system?
sentences.zh: JACK: 你觉得交通灯系统怎么样？

sentences.en: ALICE: I think supermarkets like the idea of having a colour-coded system - red, orange or green - for levels of fat, sugar and salt in a product
sentences.zh: ALICE: 我认为超市很喜欢这种用颜色编码（红色、橙色或绿色）来标示产品中脂肪、糖和盐含量水平的系统。

sentences.en: JACK: But it's not been adopted universally
sentences.zh: JACK: 但该系统并未被普遍采用。

sentences.en: And not on all products
sentences.zh: 而且并非适用于所有产品。

sentences.en: Why do you suppose & that is?
sentences.zh: 你认为这是为什么？

sentences.en: ALICE: Pressure from the food manufacturers
sentences.zh: ALICE: 来自食品制造商方面的压力。

sentences.en: Hardly surprising that some of them are opposed to flagging up how unhealthy their products are
sentences.zh: 一些制造商反对明确标示其产品不健康，这 hardly surprising（毫不奇怪）。

sentences.en: JACK: I'd have thought it would have been compulsory
sentences.zh: JACK: 我本以为这会是强制性的。

sentences.en: It seems ridiculous it isn't
sentences.zh: 看起来没做到这一点简直荒谬。

sentences.en: ALICE: I know
sentences.zh: ALICE: 我知道。

sentences.en: And what I couldn't get over is the fact that it was brought in without enough
sentences.zh: 而让我难以理解的是，该系统是在缺乏足够……的情况下推出的。

sentences.en: consultation - a lot of experts had deep reservations about it
sentences.zh: 咨询——许多专家对此深表疑虑。

sentences.en: JACK: That is a bit weird
sentences.zh: JACK: 这确实有点奇怪。

sentences.en: I suppose there's an argument for doing the research now when consumers are familiar with this system
sentences.zh: 我想，现在消费者已熟悉这一系统，倒是可以趁机开展相关研究。

sentences.en: ALICE: Yeah, maybe
sentences.zh: ALICE: 嗯，也许吧。

sentences.en: JACK: The participants in the survey were quite positive about the traffic-light system
sentences.zh: JACK: 调查参与者对交通灯系统总体评价相当积极。

sentences.en: ALICE: Mmm
sentences.zh: ALICE: 嗯。

sentences.en: But I don't think they targeted the right people
sentences.zh: 但我认为他们并未针对合适的人群。

sentences.en: They should have focused on people with low literacy levels because these labels are designed to de accessible to them
sentences.zh: 他们本应重点关注识字水平较低的人群，因为这些标签正是为便于这类人群理解而设计的。

sentences.en: JACK: Yeah
sentences.zh: JACK: 是啊。

sentences.en: But it's good to get feedback from all socio-economic groups
sentences.zh: 但能从所有社会经济群体中获取反馈仍是件好事。

sentences.en: And there wasn't & much variation in their responses
sentences.zh: 而且他们的回答差异并不大。

sentences.en: ALICE: No
sentences.zh: ALICE: 是的。

sentences.en: But if they hadn't interviewed participants face-to-face, they could have used a much bigger sample size
sentences.zh: 但如果他们没有采用面对面访谈的方式，本可以使用大得多的样本量。

sentences.en: I wonder why they chose that method?
sentences.zh: 我很好奇他们为何选择这种方法？

sentences.en: JACK: Dunno
sentences.zh: JACK: 不知道。

sentences.en: How were they selected?
sentences.zh: 这些参与者是如何选定的？

sentences.en: Did they volunteer or were they approached?
sentences.zh: 他们是自愿报名的，还是被主动邀请的？

sentences.en: ALICE: think they volunteered
sentences.zh: ALICE: 我觉得他们是自愿报名的。

sentences.en: The thing that wasn't stated was how often they bought packaged food all we know is how frequently they used the supermarket
sentences.zh: 报告中未说明的一点是：他们购买包装食品的频率；我们仅知道他们使用超市的频率。
